decision.about: How does Class.track(instance)/Class.instances() remember instances — a plain array or a WeakRef set?

options.say: A plain array, push on track()
options.why: Simplest possible code, no GC subtlety.

options.say: A Set of WeakRefs, instances() drops dead ones on read
options.why: Several classes here build throwaway instances that live one render and are dropped (Page.drew_content()'s own copy, content_at()'s preview Page) — a plain array would hold every one of those forever and only grow.

decision.because: Page is the first real user and Page instances are built throwaway in several places already (drew_content, content_at); a WeakRef set means the tracked list is always what is actually still alive, never a leak, at the cost of one extra Set/WeakRef per class (core/track/track.js).

decision.about: Where does the one-line-per-class tracking mechanism live — a tiny function each class calls once, or a mixin/base class other classes extend?

options.say: core/track/track.js exporting track(Klass) — call track(Page) once, then Page.track(this) in the constructor
options.why: Opt-in per class, one import, one call; a class that never calls it pays nothing and appears in no registry.

options.say: A Trackable base class, or track()/instances() built straight onto View so every View has it
options.why: Nothing to import per class — but every View (and everything built on it) would track by default, which the brief explicitly rules out ("don't make every class track by default").

decision.because: The requirement is opt-in per class; a shared base or a View-level default would make tracking the default instead of the exception, and most classes here should show up in no instances() list at all.

findings.text: The brief asked for the Object demo page to show the Page object, the App object and the override example at full width. `ux/Content/Object/page.js:1105-1107` shows only the override; the Page and App objects are two link rows at the bottom, below the fold at 1920 (`framework-ux-Content-Object/sheet.png`). Draw both live trees on the demo page too, and move the new section above or beside the v1 cards so it is not the last thing on the page.

The App object doesn't show "the current route and its settings" at a glance (`framework-ux-Content-Object-app/sheet.png`). It shows `.loaders .ready .socket .root .router`; the route is two clicks deep (`.router` → `.active`), and nothing on the page reads as settings. Add a hand-written `App.View` (the override the brief asked for anyway) or a summary line that states the current path and the config up front — census.md:967 already says which three fields to show.

`track` is installed but never used. `ux/Content/Object/page/page.js:1136,1145` tells the reader that `Page.track(this)` is what makes the page viewable, but the page imports `core/Page/page.js` directly and never calls `Page.instances()`, so the claim is false. Either list `Page.instances()` (count plus names, each opening into its view) or change the sentence; as it stands, deliverable 7 has no demo.

`view(thing)` picks any static named `View` (`DefaultView.js:824-825`). Nothing collides today (a grep of `framework/` finds only the demo `Widget.View`), but the code skill's "parts are static subclasses" pattern makes a `Thing.View` part used for some other job likely one day. Consider checking `Klass.View.prototype instanceof View` before using it.

Space: the Page and App trees are about 550px wide in a column that leaves 61–83% of the screen empty at 1280–3440 (`framework-ux-Content-Object-page/sheet.png`, `…-app/sheet.png`). The value column is cut at 40 characters (`DefaultView.js:817`) even where there is room for the whole value. Let the tree take `.wide` and cut to fit the row instead.

The Page object's header reads "a Doc … Page" because the instance is a Doc subclass. That's correct, but the brief expected "a Page". One word such as "a Doc (a Page)" would stop a newcomer from thinking it is the wrong object.

Navigation is clear: "The Page object" and "The App object" show as tabs on the Object module bar, and the demo page links to both. The v1 `object()` cards are kept and still reachable, as the brief required.
`ui/item/readme.md:598` says "all seven variants", but the page draws eight (`ui/item/page.js:529`). This is minion A's file, but it arrived in this diff.
No screenshot here shows `.children` expanded after a click, which the brief's "Done means" asked for. Only the closed trees are in `review/shots/`, so the lazy open is unproven from these files.

assign.title: Object views: DefaultView, track(), the Page and App objects live
assign.outcome:
**Landed — DefaultView, track(), and two real live object pages** (Phase 2, deliverables 6–9 of item-ui). `view(thing)` draws any object as a click-to-expand item tree (`ux/Content/Object/DefaultView.js`); a class overrides it with its own `Thing.View`, shown side by side with the automatic guess. `core/track/track.js`'s `track(Klass)` gives any class opt-in `Klass.track(this)` / `Klass.instances()`; `Page` now does this (one line in its constructor), so [the Page object](/framework/ux/Content/Object/page/) and [the App object](/framework/ux/Content/Object/app/) are real, live, `.children`-expandable instances, not mock-ups — proved headless, zero console errors and zero failed requests on all four pages at 1920+400.

- [x] `DefaultView` + `view()`/`Thing.View` override, both shown: [/framework/ux/Content/Object/](/framework/ux/Content/Object/)
- [x] `track()`: [core/track/track.js](/framework/core/track/track.js), wired into `Page`'s constructor
- [x] The Page object, `.children` expandable, `track()` finding 1080 live Pages: [/framework/ux/Content/Object/page/](/framework/ux/Content/Object/page/)
- [x] The App object, current route at a glance: [/framework/ux/Content/Object/app/](/framework/ux/Content/Object/app/)
- [x] `code` skill's new OOP section, linking the demo
- [x] `readme.md` + [doc/default-view.md](/framework/ux/Content/Object/doc/default-view/) updated
- [x] Reviewed (full, fresh Opus): 6 fixed, 1 declined (accepted), 2 noted — `review.md`

Left open: `ui/item/readme.md` says "seven variants", the page draws eight — flagged in the review, not fixed; that file is another minion's fence (still restyling `ui/item/`'s CSS).

Two decisions: instance storage is a `WeakRef` set, not a plain array (several classes here build throwaway instances that would otherwise leak the list forever); the tracking mechanism is a tiny opt-in function (`track(Klass)`) each class calls once, not a mixin or a base-class default, so most classes still show up in no registry at all.
